notes:
The mixed marquee for the beat that is now THE REAL DENTASOURCE, and it carries the candid team frames too: the separate Our people strip was removed on 2026-09-06 and its eighteen tiles were folded in here, so one marquee shows the crew and the work instead of two showing them apart. THIS FILE CHOOSES WHICH ITEMS, NOT WHAT ORDER THEY RUN IN. The interleave moved into mixOrder() in panels.jsx on 2026-09-06, because the training beat's strip is merged in code from two manifests and no single file can decide the order for it; two rules for the same marquee is how they drift apart. The rule is: open on a video, space the videos evenly through the whole run. Everything between the clips is a photograph. EXTENDABLE: append either type, the component re-spaces it.
☠️ FIVE FRAMES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND MUST NOT BE ADDED BACK AT TILE SIZE (ruled 2026-09-06). v033-8, v039-1, v039-2, v039-5 and v301-2 are 360 pixels wide at source with no larger copy anywhere. A tile on this strip is 384x288 css, and cover at a floor of 1.75 needs 672 across, so a 360 wide source scores min(360/384, 640/288) = 0.94 and sits visibly soft beside everything around it. They are documentary article photographs whose captions describe the exact frame, so they are never swapped for a lookalike and never upscaled. They keep their place IN the articles, where they render small; they only leave the large strips. The same five are listed in the machine readable `stripUnsafe` map on this file, keyed by filename, so a picker or a future builder can refuse them without parsing this paragraph. ☠️ NEITHER OF THESE TWO MANIFESTS IS GENERATED BY A SCRIPT: unlike crew-shots and training-media there is no builder to enforce the refusal, so the only guard is this key and whoever reads it.
☠️ tilePx IS THE DECISION NOW; THE stripUnsafe MAP BELOW IS DOCUMENTATION. tilePx is the largest CSS width a tile in this strip renders at, MEASURED on a production build at 1440 and at 390, not remembered: 384x288 css on a desktop (360x270 on a 390 phone). A file is too soft here when it cannot supply DPR 2 across that tile. The tiles are 4:3 with object-fit: cover, so the image is scaled by max(tileW/w, tileH/h) and a file passes when min(w/tileW, h/tileH) >= the floor. The floor is 1.75, not 2: it moved on 2026-09-06 so that 720 wide material clears a 384 tile. For the portrait photographs on this strip the width is the axis that binds, but the test is both axes and the long side is never the thing to compare.
☠️ TWO TILE SIZES, BECAUSE THIS IS A MIXED LIST. Measured on a production build, both marquees that use this component, both viewports:
    image tile   384x288 css desktop, 360x270 phone   (aspect-ratio 4/3)
    video tile   162x288 css desktop, 152x270 phone   (aspect-ratio 9/16)
The HEIGHT is shared, since both come from height: clamp(150px, 32vh, 300px); only the width differs, because a still is landscape in this track and a clip is portrait. So a photograph is tested against 384 and a clip against 162, and testing a clip against the image tile refuses 1280x720 landscape footage over pixels it does not need: 720 is under the image tile's 768 and well over the video tile's 324.
☠️ .dsd-reel IS NOT THE VIDEO TILE. That block in home-cinema.css carries max-width 190px and is left over from the six-vertical-reels layout the mixed marquee replaced in Q19; no component renders it and a live page has zero .dsd-reel elements, checked on both beats at both viewports. The real box is .dsd-mixed .dsd-strip-track video.
☠️ THE VIDEO ITEMS CARRY width AND height BECAUSE THE FILES NO LONGER DO. Every other manifest already did; this one did not, and it stopped mattering quietly when the video left the repo for the media origin (07befe9). The studio's guard measures a file on disk with sharp and never bars what it cannot read, so these six clips became invisible to it: not judged and passed, but not judged at all. Read off the origin with a range request against the faststart header and written here, so the guard can test them against the video tile like anything else. All six are portrait and clear the 162x288 tile comfortably, 3.33x to 4.44x against a 1.75 floor, which is why nothing changes today.
 tileFit is 'cover', measured as the computed object-fit on the rendered tile, not read off the stylesheet. ☠️ AND THE OPERATOR IS min, NOT max, WHICH THIS NOTE PREVIOUSLY HAD BACKWARDS. There are two forms and they are reciprocals, so it is easy to state the wrong one: the SCALE to cover is max(tileW/w, tileH/h), and the RESOLUTION RATIO is its reciprocal, min(w/tileW, h/tileH), which is the form every implementation uses. A cover tile crops to fill, so the axis that fills first is the one that must supply the pixels, and it is the SMALLER of the two ratios that decides. contain is the other way round, max of the ratios, which is what parts.json takes. A 'contain' tile would letterbox instead and need less, which is why the parts rows are a different case and not merely a smaller one.
